Secondary 11th Chords · Level 1.heading: Hear the full chord. Choose its type.
Secondary 11th Chords · Level 1.intro: You will hear a chord with an eleventh or a raised eleventh and a different combination of chord notes. Choose the name that matches its sound.

steps.title: Listen to the whole chord
steps.description: Press Play and listen to the notes together. Focus on the sound of the whole chord rather than trying to name every note. You can listen again whenever you need to.

steps.title: Choose the chord type
steps.description: Choose the chord name that matches what you hear. The four answer names show the different combinations of chord notes used in this lesson.

steps.title: Submit your answer
steps.description: When you are ready, press Submit Answer. You can change your choice before you submit.

Secondary 11th Chords · Level 1.about: These chords use an eleventh or a raised eleventh with different combinations of chord notes. For example, F minor-major eleventh uses F, A♭, C, E, G and B♭: a minor three-note chord with a major seventh, ninth and eleventh added. In the answer names, ♯5 means a raised fifth, ♯11 means a raised eleventh, and ♭9 means a lowered ninth. Raising or lowering a note means moving one keyboard step, counting both white and black keys. This lesson uses chords built on F. The root, the note the chord is named after, stays at the bottom. Choose only the chord type; there is no separate inversion answer.
Secondary 11th Chords · Level 1.layoutCaption: F minor-major eleventh, with all six chord notes played together.
Secondary 11th Chords · Level 1.exampleExplanation: This visual example is F minor-major eleventh. Choose Minor-Major 11th. During the quiz, choose the chord type you hear, even when the notes are arranged differently.
